# Model and source

Masters 2026 characterises the population pharmacokinetics (PK) of
**sasanlimab** (PF-06801591), a subcutaneously (SC) administered anti-PD-1
IgG4 monoclonal antibody, and its exposure-response (ER) relationships for
safety and efficacy. The work supports the flat 300 mg SC every-4-weeks (Q4W)
dose in BCG-naive, high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC).

- Citation: Masters JC, Jermain B, Liu A, Cesari R, Calella AM, Michelon E,
  Wei C, Liu S, Piscitelli J. Population Pharmacokinetics and
  Exposure-Response of Sasanlimab, a Checkpoint Inhibitor, in Patients with
  Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer and Other Solid Tumors. *J Clin
  Pharmacol.* 2026;66(9):e70295.
- Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.70295>

The paper reports seven models, packaged as seven files that share this
article:

```{r models}
models <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,                                   ~endpoint,                                    ~source,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab",                "Serum sasanlimab concentration (popPK)",     "Table 3; Equations S1, S2",
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade2",    "Any grade >= 2 TEAE",                        "Table 4 slope; Figure S2 intercept",
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade3",    "Any grade >= 3 TEAE",                        "Table 4 slope; Figure S2 intercept",
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae",           "Any-grade immune-related AE",                "Table 4 slope; Figure S2 intercept",
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae_grade3",    "Grade >= 3 immune-related AE",               "Table 4 slope; Figure S2 intercept",
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_cr",             "Investigator-assessed complete response",    "Table S5",
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_efs",            "Investigator-assessed event-free survival",  "Table S4"
)
mods <- lapply(
  stats::setNames(models$model, models$model),
  function(m) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))
)
knitr::kable(models, caption = "Models contributed by Masters 2026.")
```

# Population

The population PK and the ER-safety analyses pool the same 1007 participants
from three studies (Masters 2026 Table 1): B8011001 (n = 146, phase 1 dose
escalation with IV 0.5-10 mg/kg Q3W and SC 300 mg Q4W, plus NSCLC and
urothelial carcinoma expansion cohorts), B8011006 (CREST, n = 706, NMIBC,
sasanlimab 300 mg SC Q4W combined with BCG in 698) and B8011007 (n = 155,
SC 300 mg Q4W or 600 mg Q6W). The pooled cohort's median age was 66 years
(range 26-90) and its median weight 74 kg (range 38.2-173); 21.8% were
female, and 70.1% had NMIBC, 19.7% NSCLC, 3.9% urothelial carcinoma and
6.4% other solid tumors (Supporting Tables S1 and S2).

The ER-efficacy analyses use CREST Cohort A only: 698 participants for
event-free survival (EFS; arm A, sasanlimab + BCG induction + maintenance,
n = 350; arm B, sasanlimab + BCG induction only, n = 348) and the 179 with
carcinoma in situ (CIS) at randomization for complete response (CR).

```{r population}
pop_rows <- lapply(models$model, function(m) {
  p <- readModelDb(m)()$population
  tibble::tibble(
    model = m,
    n_subjects = p$n_subjects,
    disease = substr(p$disease_state, 1, 90)
  )
})
knitr::kable(dplyr::bind_rows(pop_rows), caption = "Analysis populations.")
```

# Population PK

## Virtual NMIBC cohort

The virtual cohort resembles the CREST participants (B8011006 column of
Supporting Table S1): body weight log-normal with mean 78.1 kg and SD
17.3 kg; serum creatinine log-normal around a median of 0.9 mg/dL; albumin
normal with mean 4.4 g/dL and SD 0.3; alkaline phosphatase log-normal with
median 76.2 U/L and mean 87.4 U/L. All tumor-type indicators are 0 (NMIBC is
the reference). Albumin is supplied in the canonical g/L.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261123)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261123)
n_pk <- 200

lnorm_from_mean_sd <- function(n, mean, sd) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (sd / mean)^2))
  stats::rlnorm(n, log(mean) - sdlog^2 / 2, sdlog)
}
clamp <- function(x, lo, hi) pmin(pmax(x, lo), hi)

cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_pk),
  WT = clamp(lnorm_from_mean_sd(n_pk, 78.07, 17.31), 40.5, 173),
  CREAT = clamp(stats::rlnorm(n_pk, log(0.9), 0.22), 0.4, 2.0),
  ALB = 10 * clamp(stats::rnorm(n_pk, 4.4, 0.3), 3.0, 5.5),
  ALP = clamp(stats::rlnorm(n_pk, log(76.2), sqrt(2 * log(87.4 / 76.2))), 31, 1132),
  TUMTP_NSCLC = 0, TUMTP_BLADDER = 0, TUMTP_OTHER = 0,
  treatment = "300 mg SC Q4W"
)
summary(cohort[, c("WT", "CREAT", "ALB", "ALP")])
```

## Simulation: 300 mg SC Q4W for one year

Twelve doses; half-day sampling over the first interval (single dose) and over
the twelfth interval (days 308-336), by which point the 29-day half-life has
elapsed more than ten times. The SC dose record carries `rate = -2` so the
model's duration `D1` applies.

```{r simulate-pk}
dose_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = seq(0, 308, by = 28)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 300, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", rate = -2)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 28, by = 0.5), seq(308, 336, by = 0.5))))
obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = obs_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
ev_pk <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(cohort, by = "id")

sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mods$Masters_2026_sasanlimab, events = ev_pk,
  keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r fig-conc, fig.cap = "Simulated serum sasanlimab after the first dose and over the twelfth dose interval (median and 5th-95th percentiles of individual predictions). Compare with the Q4W panel of Figure 2 of Masters 2026."}
sim_pk |>
  dplyr::mutate(interval = ifelse(time <= 28, "Dose 1 (days 0-28)", "Dose 12 (days 308-336)")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(interval, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = stats::median(Cc), lo = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    hi = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  facet_wrap(~interval, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Sasanlimab (ug/mL)")
```

## Half-life and volume at steady state

Masters 2026 reports a mean elimination half-life of about 29 days and a
geometric-mean steady-state volume of 6.34 L (Results).

```{r half-life}
indiv <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl, vc, q, vp) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    k10 = cl / vc, k12 = q / vc, k21 = q / vp,
    beta = 0.5 * ((k10 + k12 + k21) - sqrt((k10 + k12 + k21)^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)),
    thalf = log(2) / beta,
    vss = vc + vp
  )
hl_check <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("Mean terminal half-life (day)", "Geometric-mean Vss (L)"),
  simulated = c(mean(indiv$thalf), exp(mean(log(indiv$vss)))),
  published = c(29, 6.34)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))
knitr::kable(hl_check, digits = 2, caption = "Derived disposition vs Results text.")
stopifnot(abs(hl_check$pct_diff) < 15)
```

## PKNCA: first-dose and steady-state exposure

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- dose_rows |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "300 mg SC Q4W") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
# PKNCA returns ctrough only when a dose follows the interval, so the
# steady-state trough is taken as cmin: after an SC dose the interval minimum
# is the end-of-interval concentration.
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 308), end = c(28, 336),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cav = TRUE,
  ctrough = c(TRUE, FALSE), cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)
```

The published references are the Cohort A exposure summary (Supporting Table
S3, NMIBC on 300 mg SC Q4W, n = 698) for the first-dose Cavg and Ctrough, and
the median reference lines of Figure S2 (pooled ER-safety cohort, n = 1007,
digitised) for the first-dose Cmax and the steady-state Cmax and Ctrough. The
pooled cohort includes the higher-clearance non-NMIBC tumor types, the IV
dose-escalation regimens and 600 mg Q6W, so its medians are only
approximately comparable with the NMIBC cohort simulated here.

```{r nca-compare}
nca_sd <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(start == 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Dose 1 (days 0-28)")
nca_ss <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(start == 308) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    treatment = "Steady state (days 308-336)",
    PPTESTCD = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "cmin", "ctrough", PPTESTCD)
  )
nca_both <- dplyr::bind_rows(nca_sd, nca_ss) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cav", "ctrough"))

published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                     ~cmax, ~cav,  ~ctrough,
  "Dose 1 (days 0-28)",           27.1,  21.8,  18.3,
  "Steady state (days 308-336)",  53.8,  NA,    33.4
)

sim_wide <- nca_both |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_wide |> dplyr::select(-id),
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", cav = "ug/mL", ctrough = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  nca_cmp,
  caption = "Simulated median exposure vs Masters 2026 Table S3 and Figure S2. * differs by > 20%."
)
```

```{r nca-gate}
med_sim <- sim_wide |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(cmax, cav, ctrough), stats::median), .groups = "drop")
gate <- med_sim |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-treatment, names_to = "param", values_to = "sim") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(published_nca, -treatment, names_to = "param", values_to = "pub"),
    by = c("treatment", "param")
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(pub)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (sim / pub - 1))
# The NMIBC-only Table S3 values (Cavg,sd and Ctrough,sd) are the like-for-like
# comparison; a mis-transcribed clearance, F or D1 moves them by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(gate$pct[gate$treatment == "Dose 1 (days 0-28)" & gate$param %in% c("cav", "ctrough")]) < 10),
  all(abs(gate$pct) < 20)
)
```

Supporting Table S3 also reports the Cavg,sd range in Cohort A (5.2-38.0
ug/mL, SD 5.63) and Figure 4 the quartile medians 15.2, 19.9, 23.7 and 28.6
ug/mL:

```{r cavg-quartiles}
cav_sd <- sim_wide |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "Dose 1 (days 0-28)")
q_cut <- stats::quantile(cav_sd$cav, c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))
quart <- cav_sd |>
  dplyr::mutate(quartile = cut(cav, q_cut, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = paste0("Q", 1:4))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(quartile) |>
  dplyr::summarise(simulated_median = stats::median(cav), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(published_median = c(15.2, 19.9, 23.7, 28.6))
knitr::kable(quart, digits = 1, caption = "Cavg,sd quartile medians vs Figure 4 legend.")
```

## Body-weight effect and flat dosing (Figures 1 and 3)

Figure 1 summarises steady-state Cavg by body-weight quartile relative to the
overall median: 1.29, 1.10, 0.976 and 0.788 for quartiles 1-4. Figure 3
compares flat 300 mg with weight-based 4 mg/kg dosing; because the PK is
linear, the weight-based Cavg is the flat Cavg scaled by 4 x WT / 300.

```{r weight-quartiles}
cav_ss <- sim_wide |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "Steady state (days 308-336)") |>
  dplyr::left_join(cohort |> dplyr::select(id, WT), by = "id")
wq <- stats::quantile(cav_ss$WT, c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))
wt_tab <- cav_ss |>
  dplyr::mutate(wt_quartile = cut(WT, wq, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = paste0("Q", 1:4))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(wt_quartile) |>
  dplyr::summarise(simulated_ratio = stats::median(cav) / stats::median(cav_ss$cav), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(published_ratio = c(1.29, 1.10, 0.976, 0.788))
knitr::kable(wt_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Cavg,ss by body-weight quartile relative to the median (Figure 1).")
# The weight exponent on CL (0.980) fixes the spread between the outer
# quartiles; a wrong reference weight or a dropped exponent collapses it.
stopifnot(
  wt_tab$simulated_ratio[1] > 1.1, wt_tab$simulated_ratio[4] < 0.9,
  abs(wt_tab$simulated_ratio[1] / wt_tab$simulated_ratio[4] - 1.29 / 0.788) < 0.4
)
```

```{r fig-flat-dose, fig.cap = "Steady-state Cavg by body-weight quartile for flat 300 mg and weight-based 4 mg/kg SC Q4W. Replicates the right panel of Figure 3 of Masters 2026."}
cav_ss |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    wt_quartile = cut(WT, wq, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = c("0-25th", "25-50th", "50-75th", "75-100th")),
    `Flat 300 mg` = cav,
    `4 mg/kg` = cav * 4 * WT / 300
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`Flat 300 mg`, `4 mg/kg`), names_to = "regimen", values_to = "cavg") |>
  ggplot(aes(wt_quartile, cavg, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6) +
  labs(x = "Body-weight percentile", y = "Cavg,ss (ug/mL)", fill = NULL)
```

## Tumor type

The (1 + Tumor Type) factor of Equation S1 raises CL by 33.2% (NSCLC), 31.0%
(urothelial carcinoma) and 10.8% (other tumors) over NMIBC. For a linear
model the steady-state Cavg of a typical patient scales as 1 / CL:

```{r tumor-type}
typ_cav <- function(nsclc, bladder, other) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 300, cmt = "depot", rate = -2, ii = 28, addl = 11) |>
    rxode2::et(seq(308, 336, by = 0.25), cmt = "central") |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      WT = 70, CREAT = 0.9, ALB = 43, ALP = 80,
      TUMTP_NSCLC = nsclc, TUMTP_BLADDER = bladder, TUMTP_OTHER = other
    )
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mods$Masters_2026_sasanlimab), events = ev))
  s <- s[s$time >= 308, ]
  sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2) / 28
}
tt <- tibble::tibble(
  tumor = c("NMIBC", "NSCLC", "Urothelial carcinoma", "Other"),
  cav_ss = c(typ_cav(0, 0, 0), typ_cav(1, 0, 0), typ_cav(0, 1, 0), typ_cav(0, 0, 1))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ratio_vs_nmibc = cav_ss / cav_ss[1],
    expected = 1 / (1 + c(0, 0.332, 0.310, 0.108))
  )
knitr::kable(tt, digits = 3, caption = "Typical-patient steady-state Cavg by tumor type.")
# Same drawn parameters on both sides (typical values): pure numerical check.
stopifnot(max(abs(tt$ratio_vs_nmibc - tt$expected)) < 0.005)
```

The forest plot of Figure 1 shows these ratios against the pooled median
rather than against NMIBC, and folds in each group's own covariate
distribution, so its values (NSCLC 0.872, UC 0.902, other 0.950, NMIBC 1.05)
are compressed relative to the typical-patient ratios above.

# Exposure-safety models

## The intercepts are reconstructed from Figure S2

Table 4 prints only the exposure slope of each final ER-safety model. No
intercept and no covariate coefficient appears anywhere in the paper, yet the
Methods describe a full-covariate model followed by backward elimination. The
maintainers digitised the fitted curves of Supporting Figure S2 (500 curve
points per panel, axes calibrated on the gridlines). With the slope left free
the curves return slopes of 0.1233 (TEAE >= 2), -0.3444 (TEAE >= 3) and
-0.0784 (irAE any grade) against the printed 0.123, -0.344 and -0.0788, so
the figure is the published model; the intercepts were then estimated with
the slope held at its printed value. The irAE grade >= 3 curve sits at
probabilities 0.03-0.17, where one pixel moves the logit by up to 0.1; its
free slope (0.0079) is within that resolution of the printed 0.00713.

The table checks each packaged model against the curve at the 5th, 50th and
95th percentile exposure lines of the same figure.

```{r safety-curve-check}
safety <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,                                 ~output,             ~cov,       ~log_axis,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade2",  "prob_teae_grade2",  "CMAX",     TRUE,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade3",  "prob_teae_grade3",  "CMAX",     TRUE,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae",         "prob_irae",         "CTROUGH",  TRUE,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae_grade3",  "prob_irae_grade3",  "CMAX",     FALSE
)
# Figure S2 axis value at the 5th / 50th / 95th percentile line and the
# digitised curve probability there.
digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,                                 ~axis_x, ~p_fig,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade2",  2.705,   0.779,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade2",  3.300,   0.794,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade2",  4.007,   0.807,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade3",  3.348,   0.494,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade3",  3.986,   0.439,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade3",  4.488,   0.396,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae",         2.571,   0.241,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae",         3.507,   0.228,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae",         4.028,   0.222,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae_grade3",  15.22,   0.028,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae_grade3",  27.43,   0.031,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae_grade3",  55.15,   0.040
)

solve_prob <- function(model, output, cov, values) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = seq_along(values), time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0L)
  ev[[cov]] <- values
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[model]], events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"))[[output]]
}

curve_chk <- digitised |>
  dplyr::left_join(safety, by = "model") |>
  dplyr::group_by(model) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    exposure = ifelse(log_axis, exp(axis_x), axis_x),
    p_model = solve_prob(model[1], output[1], cov[1], exposure)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(model, exposure, p_fig, p_model)
knitr::kable(curve_chk, digits = 3, caption = "Packaged models vs the digitised Figure S2 curves.")
# Same curve on both sides (no cohort): a digitisation-resolution bound.
stopifnot(max(abs(curve_chk$p_model - curve_chk$p_fig)) < 0.01)
```

```{r fig-safety, fig.cap = "Packaged exposure-safety models over the plotted exposure ranges, with the 5th, 50th and 95th percentile exposures as dashed lines. Replicates Figure S2 of Masters 2026 (axes as in the source: natural log of exposure, except irAE grade >= 3)."}
ranges <- list(
  Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade2 = c(1.1, 5.5),
  Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade3 = c(2.1, 6.15),
  Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae = c(-0.45, 5.45),
  Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae_grade3 = c(3, 257)
)
curves <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(safety)), function(i) {
  s <- safety[i, ]
  x <- seq(ranges[[s$model]][1], ranges[[s$model]][2], length.out = 100)
  tibble::tibble(
    model = s$model, axis_x = x,
    p = solve_prob(s$model, s$output, s$cov, if (s$log_axis) exp(x) else x)
  )
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
ggplot(curves, aes(axis_x, p)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  geom_vline(data = digitised, aes(xintercept = axis_x), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free_x") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Exposure (log ug/mL; ug/mL for irAE grade >= 3)", y = "Predicted probability")
```

## Which population the curves describe

A logistic regression with an intercept reproduces the observed event rate of
the data it was fitted to. The curves of Figure S2 do not reproduce the
pooled incidence for the two irAE endpoints, so the final models contain
covariate terms that are not printed, and the figure is drawn at their
reference levels. The table compares each curve at its median exposure with
the observed incidences of Supporting Table S6.

```{r safety-strata}
obs_inc <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,                                 ~pooled, ~non_nmibc, ~nmibc,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade2",  0.846,   (117 + 123) / 301, 0.867,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_teae_grade3",  0.434,   (61 + 60) / 301,   0.448,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae",         0.546,   (47 + 30) / 301,   0.670,
  "Masters_2026_sasanlimab_irae_grade3",  0.152,   (8 + 6) / 301,     0.197
)
strata <- curve_chk |>
  dplyr::group_by(model) |>
  dplyr::slice(2) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(model, p_model_at_median = p_model) |>
  dplyr::left_join(obs_inc, by = "model")
knitr::kable(
  strata, digits = 3,
  caption = paste(
    "Curve at the median exposure vs observed incidence: pooled (n = 1007),",
    "B8011001 + B8011007 (non-NMIBC monotherapy, n = 301) and B8011006",
    "(NMIBC + BCG, n = 706)."
  )
)
```

The curves track the non-NMIBC monotherapy incidence (B8011001 + B8011007)
within a few points for every endpoint. For the irAE endpoints they sit far
below the NMIBC + BCG incidence (0.23 vs 0.67; 0.03 vs 0.20), so the packaged
irAE models apply to non-NMIBC monotherapy only. In this cohort tumor type
NMIBC, study B8011006 and BCG combination coincide (706 / 706 / 698 of 1007),
so the omitted term is most likely one of them, but its coefficient is not
reported.

# Exposure-efficacy: complete response

The CR model (Supporting Table S5) is driven by Cavg,sd. Applied to the
first-dose Cavg of the simulated NMIBC cohort, it should give close to the
observed "nearly 90%" CR rate in the 179 participants with CIS.

```{r cr}
cr_ev <- data.frame(id = cav_sd$id, time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0L, CAV = cav_sd$cav)
cr_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mods$Masters_2026_sasanlimab_cr, events = cr_ev))
cr_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("Mean predicted CR probability (simulated cohort)", "P(CR) at Cavg,sd = 21.8 ug/mL (Table S3 median)"),
  value = c(mean(cr_sim$prob_cr_investigator), stats::plogis(3.72 - 0.0670 * 21.8))
)
knitr::kable(cr_tab, digits = 3)
stopifnot(abs(mean(cr_sim$prob_cr_investigator) - 0.90) < 0.03)
```

```{r fig-cr, fig.cap = "Probability of investigator-assessed CR against Cavg,sd, with the simulated cohort's Cavg,sd distribution as a rug."}
cr_curve <- data.frame(id = 1:100, time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0L, CAV = seq(5, 40, length.out = 100))
as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mods$Masters_2026_sasanlimab_cr, events = cr_curve)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(CAV = cr_curve$CAV) |>
  ggplot(aes(CAV, prob_cr_investigator)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_rug(data = cav_sd, aes(x = cav), inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.4) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Cavg,sd (ug/mL)", y = "P(complete response)")
```

# Exposure-efficacy: event-free survival

The EFS model is a log-normal time-to-event model without an exposure term.
The virtual Cohort A has 200 participants per arm, with age normal (mean 66.4
years, SD 10.1, range 31-90) and weight log-normal (mean 78.1 kg, SD 17.3) as
in the B8011006 column of Table S1. The population-averaged event-free
probability is compared with the midpoints of the 95% simulation band of the
visual predictive check in Supporting Figure S4 (digitised by the
maintainers).

```{r efs}
n_arm <- 200
efs_cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(2 * n_arm),
  BCG_MAINT = rep(c(1, 0), each = n_arm),
  AGE = clamp(stats::rnorm(2 * n_arm, 66.4, 10.1), 31, 90),
  WT = clamp(lnorm_from_mean_sd(2 * n_arm, 78.07, 17.31), 40.5, 173)
)
efs_times <- c(0, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48)
efs_ev <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = efs_cohort$id, time = efs_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L) |>
  dplyr::left_join(efs_cohort, by = "id")
efs_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mods$Masters_2026_sasanlimab_efs, events = efs_ev, keep = "BCG_MAINT"
))

efs_pop <- efs_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(simulated = mean(sur), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      time = c(3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48),
      figure_s4_mid = c(0.958, 0.923, 0.873, 0.832, 0.800, 0.773, 0.741, 0.729, 0.711)
    ),
    by = "time"
  )
knitr::kable(efs_pop, digits = 3, caption = "Population-averaged EFS vs the Figure S4 simulation band (midpoint).")
# Envelope on the population average: the band is +/- about 0.02 wide, and the
# additive-on-mu reading of the covariates runs about 0.05 high.
stopifnot(max(abs(efs_pop$simulated - efs_pop$figure_s4_mid)) < 0.03)
```

```{r fig-efs, fig.cap = "Population-averaged event-free probability by arm (arm A: BCG induction + maintenance; arm B: induction only), with the Figure S4 band midpoints as points."}
efs_sim |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = ifelse(BCG_MAINT == 1, "Arm A (maintenance)", "Arm B (induction only)")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sur = mean(sur), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, sur, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = efs_pop, aes(time, figure_s4_mid), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Time (months)", y = "P(event-free)", colour = NULL)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Safety-model intercepts are figure-derived.** Table 4 prints only the
  exposure slope of each ER-safety model. The intercepts (0.935, 1.125,
  -0.942, -3.51) were digitised by the maintainers from Supporting Figure S2
  with the slope held at its printed value. The final models also contain
  covariate terms whose coefficients are not reported; the packaged models
  reproduce the curves as plotted, which match the incidence of the
  non-NMIBC monotherapy studies (B8011001 + B8011007). They under-predict
  patients with NMIBC treated with sasanlimab + BCG, markedly so for the irAE
  endpoints.
- **Safety and CR likelihoods.** The source models are Bernoulli logistic
  regressions with no residual error and no random effect. Each packaged
  model carries a fixed additive residual SD of 0.001 on the probability
  only so that rxode2 has an error model; it is not a published quantity.
- **EFS covariate forms.** Table S4 gives the coefficients but not the
  equations. The Methods state that the stepwise covariate modelling tested
  continuous covariates as linear, exponential or power functions and
  categorical ones linearly. The packaged form is the multiplicative
  parameterisation of PsN stepwise covariate modelling: age linear centred
  at 67 years, weight as a power normalised to 76 kg (the B8011006 medians in
  Table S1; the EFS-set medians are not reported), arm as 1 + theta x
  indicator. With these forms and time in months the population-averaged
  curve reproduces the Figure S4 band, while an additive-on-mu reading runs
  about five points high.
- **EFS arm direction.** The paper does not print the arm coding; the
  Results state that receiving BCG induction + maintenance is beneficial to
  EFS, so the -0.144 coefficient is applied to arm B (`BCG_MAINT = 0`).
- **IIV covariance.** The Table 3 row 'wCL/V2 Correlation' (0.0625, 'CV'
  25% = sqrt(0.0625)) is read as the CL-V2 covariance, consistent with the
  squared notation of the other omega rows; the implied correlation is 0.36.
- **Albumin units.** Equation S1 normalises albumin to 4.3 g/dL; the model
  takes albumin in the canonical g/L and divides by 10 internally.
- **Tumor-type coding.** NMIBC is the reference level. Participants with
  NMIBC carry `TUMTP_BLADDER = 0`; that indicator marks the advanced
  urothelial carcinoma cohort only.
- **IV dosing.** The B8011001 IV doses (0.5-10 mg/kg over 60 minutes Q3W) go
  to `central` as an infusion with the rate set in the data; F and D1 apply
  to SC doses into `depot` only.
- **Reference exposures in the PKNCA comparison.** The first-dose Cmax and
  steady-state Cmax and Ctrough references are the median lines of Figure
  S2, read from the pooled ER-safety cohort (all regimens and tumor types),
  not from the NMIBC 300 mg Q4W cohort simulated here.
- **Virtual-cohort covariates.** Distributions follow the B8011006 summary
  statistics of Table S1 (log-normal weight, creatinine and alkaline
  phosphatase; normal albumin and age), independent of each other.
